description: Proving general trigonometric/complex-number identities that hold for an arbitrary parameter (\theta, \alpha \in \mathbb{R} and n \in \mathbb{Z}), using the trigonometric form z=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta and De Moivre's formula, rather than computing a single numeric power.

source.description: Cambodian BAC II grade-12 math textbook, Chapter 2 (complex numbers, trigonometric form / powers / roots) — exercises only
source.extracted_by: manual OCR/transcription from scanned textbook (Claude Code), 2026-08-25

exercises.technique: Recognize numerator/denominator as conjugates of equal modulus; rewrite 1+\sin\theta \pm i\cos\theta in trig form using complementary-angle identities, form the quotient (a unit-modulus complex number), then apply De Moivre's formula.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } z=\cos\alpha+i\sin\alpha \text{ and } w=\frac{2z^5}{1+z^4}, \text{ where } \alpha\in\left(-\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{\pi}{4}\right). \text{ Prove that } w = \frac{1}{\cos 2\alpha}(\cos 3\alpha + i\sin 3\alpha).
exercises.technique: Factor z^{5/2} out of numerator and denominator (dividing top and bottom by z^2), express 1+z^4 in terms of z^2 = \cos2\alpha+i\sin2\alpha using the identity z^{-2}+z^2 = 2\cos2\alpha, and simplify using De Moivre's formula.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } Z = \cos\alpha + i\sin\alpha, \text{ where } \alpha\in\mathbb{R}. \text{ For } n\in\mathbb{Z}, \text{ prove that } z^n + \frac{1}{z^n} = 2\cos(n\alpha).
exercises.technique: Apply De Moivre's formula to z^n and to 1/z^n = z^{-n} (using \cos(-n\alpha)=\cos(n\alpha), \sin(-n\alpha)=-\sin(n\alpha)), then add — the imaginary parts cancel.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } z=a+ib \text{ and } A=i(1+z). \text{ Calculate } A \text{ as a function of } a \text{ and } b, \text{ writing the result in algebraic form.}
\text{Determine } a \text{ and } b \text{ such that } A = z, \text{ where } A=i(1+z), z=a+ib.
exercises.technique: Set the algebraic form of A equal to a+ib and equate real and imaginary parts to obtain a system in a, b.
